% ---- convexity
\cssec{Convexity tests}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Convex set} $C$: $(1-t)x + ty \in C$ for all $x, y \in C$ and $t \in [0, 1]$. \textbf{Convex function} (the Jensen inequality): $f\big((1-t)x + ty\big) \le (1-t)f(x) + t f(y)$.
  \item \textbf{First order} ($f \in C^1$): $f$ is convex $\iff f(y) \ge f(x) + \nabla f(x)^\top (y - x)$ for all $x, y$; the tangent lies below the graph. For $f(x) = x^2$: $f(\val{ex.first.y}) = \val{ex.first.fy} \ge f(\val{ex.first.x}) + f'(\val{ex.first.x})(\val{ex.first.y} - \val{ex.first.x}) = \val{ex.first.tangent}$.
  \item \textbf{Second order} ($f \in C^2$): $f$ is convex $\iff \nabla^2 f(x) \succeq 0$ at every $x$; $\nabla^2 f \succ 0$ everywhere implies strict convexity (not conversely). $H \succeq 0$: all eigenvalues $\ge 0$, or \textbf{all} principal minors $\ge 0$; $H \succ 0$: leading minors $> 0$. A1: $f = \val{A1.tex.f}$ has $H_{11} = \val{A1.steps.minor11}$, $H_{22} = \val{A1.steps.minor22}$, $\det H = \val{A1.tex.det}$, so $f$ is convex $\iff |a| \le \val{A1.params.aEdge}$.
  \item \textbf{One violating pair disproves} convexity; passing random tests proves nothing. A2: $f = \val{A2.tex.f}$, $p = \val{A2.params.p}$, $q = \val{A2.params.q}$: $f(p) = f(q) = 0$, but $f\big(\tfrac{p+q}{2}\big) = \val{A2.tex.fm} > 0$.
\end{itemize}

% ---- sets
\cssec{What preserves convexity}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Intersections} $\bigcap_\alpha C_\alpha$ of convex sets are convex; \textbf{unions} in general are not (two disjoint disks).
  \item \textbf{Sublevel set} $\{x:\ f(x) \le \alpha\}$ of a convex $f$ is convex; for a nonconvex $f$ check the set itself: $S = \val{A3.tex.S}$ is not convex. \textbf{Epigraph} $\operatorname{epi} f = \{(x, s):\ f(x) \le s\}$ is convex $\iff f$ is convex.
  \item \textbf{Affine maps}: the image $\{Ax + b:\ x \in C\}$ and the preimage $\{x:\ Ax + b \in C\}$ of a convex set are convex. Convex: half-spaces, balls, boxes, $\Delta_d = \{x \in \mathbb R^d:\ x \ge 0,\ \mathbf 1^\top x = 1\}$.
  \item The feasible set $\{g_i \le 0,\ h_j = 0\}$ with convex $g_i$ and affine $h_j$ is convex. A3: $T = \val{A3.tex.T}$ is a disk intersected with an epigraph, hence convex.
\end{itemize}

% ---- projections
\cssec{Projections}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Projection} $P_C(x) = \arg\min_{y \in C} \|y - x\|$; for a closed convex $C$ it exists and is unique.
  \item \textbf{Ball} $\{\|y - c\| \le r\}$: $P(x) = c + r\,(x - c)/\max(r,\ \|x - c\|)$. \textbf{Box} $[l, u]$: $P(x) = \min(\max(x, l), u)$ coordinatewise. B2: $x = \val{B2.params.x}$ goes to $\val{B2.steps.ball}$ on the unit ball and to $\val{B2.steps.box}$ on the box $[\val{B2.params.lo}, \val{B2.params.hi}]^2$.
  \item \textbf{Probability simplex} $\Delta_d$: sort $v$ in decreasing order into $u$; $s_j = u_1 + \dots + u_j$; $\rho = \max\{j:\ u_j - (s_j - 1)/j > 0\}$; $\theta = (s_\rho - 1)/\rho$; $P(v) = \max(v - \theta,\ 0)$ in the \textbf{original} order. B3: $v = \val{B3.params.v}$, $u = \val{B3.steps.u}$, $s = \val{B3.steps.s}$, $\rho = \val{B3.steps.rho}$, $\theta = \val{B3.steps.theta}$, $P(v) = \val{B3.steps.x}$.
  \item \textbf{Obtuse angle}: $p = P_C(x) \iff p \in C$ and $(x - p)^\top (y - p) \le 0$ for all $y \in C$, i.e. $x - p$ lies in the normal cone $N_C(p)$. On $\Delta_d$ it suffices to test the vertices $y = e_k$.
\end{itemize}

% ---- kkt
\cssec{KKT conditions}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Problem: $\min f(x)$ subject to $g_i(x) \le 0$, $h_j(x) = 0$. Lagrangian: $\mathcal L(x, \lambda, \nu) = f(x) + \sum_i \lambda_i g_i(x) + \sum_j \nu_j h_j(x)$ with $\lambda \ge 0$ and $\nu$ of any sign.
  \item \textbf{Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) conditions} at $x^*$. \emph{Stationarity}: $\nabla_x \mathcal L = \nabla f + \sum_i \lambda_i \nabla g_i + \sum_j \nu_j \nabla h_j = 0$. \emph{Primal feasibility}: $g_i(x^*) \le 0$, $h_j(x^*) = 0$. \emph{Dual feasibility}: $\lambda_i \ge 0$. \emph{Complementary slackness}: $\lambda_i g_i(x^*) = 0$.
  \item \textbf{Signs}: write every inequality as $g \le 0$ and add $+\lambda g$ to $\mathcal L$ with $\lambda \ge 0$; $x_1 \ge 0$ becomes $-x_1 \le 0$. SciPy writes inequalities as $c(x) \ge 0$: pass $c = -g$.
  \item \textbf{Geometry}: \[-\nabla f(x^*) = \sum_{i\ \text{active}} \lambda_i \nabla g_i + \sum_j \nu_j \nabla h_j,\] the antigradient lies in the cone of the active gradients, which under Slater's condition is the normal cone $N_C(x^*) = \{s:\ s^\top (y - x^*) \le 0\ \forall y \in C\}$. C1: $\min \val{C1.tex.f}$ subject to $\val{C1.tex.g} \le 0$ gives $x^* = \val{C1.answer.x.value}$, $\lambda^* = \val{C1.answer.lam.value}$ and $-\nabla f(x^*) = \val{C1.steps.minusGrad} = \val{C1.answer.lam.value} \cdot \val{C1.params.A.1}$.
\end{itemize}

% ---- active
\cssec{Active constraints}
\begin{itemize}
  \item A constraint is \textbf{active} at $x^*$ if $g_i(x^*) = 0$ and \textbf{inactive} if $g_i(x^*) < 0$; equalities are always active.
  \item Complementary slackness: inactive $\Rightarrow \lambda_i = 0$; $\lambda_i > 0 \Rightarrow$ active. An active constraint \textbf{may} have $\lambda_i = 0$.
  \item \textbf{Active-set search}: guess the active set; solve stationarity with $g_i = 0$ for active $i$ and $\lambda_i = 0$ for the rest; keep the candidate only if $g(x) \le 0$ and $\lambda \ge 0$. A negative $\lambda_i$ means a wrong active set.
  \item C2: $\min \val{C2.tex.f}$ subject to $\val{C2.tex.g} \le 0$. The case $\lambda = 0$ gives $x^* = \val{C2.answer.x.value}$ with $g = \val{C2.steps.gStar} < 0$, so $\lambda^* = 0$. Assuming $g = 0$ gives $\lambda = \val{C2.cand.S1.lam.1} < 0$: rejected.
  \item A multiplier is a price: relaxing $g_i \le 0$ to $g_i \le u_i$ changes the optimal value at the rate $\partial p^*/\partial u_i = -\lambda_i^*$.
\end{itemize}

% ---- slater
\cssec{Slater's condition}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Slater's condition}: the problem is convex ($f$, $g_i$ convex, $h_j$ affine) and has a strictly feasible point: $g_i(\bar x) < 0$, $h_j(\bar x) = 0$. C1: $\bar x = \val{ex.slater.point}$, $g(\bar x) = \val{ex.slater.g} < 0$.
  \item In a convex problem every KKT point is a global minimum; with a Slater point the converse holds too: every minimum has multipliers.
  \item \textbf{Without a constraint qualification KKT may fail}: $\min x$ subject to $x^2 \le 0$. Only $x^* = \val{D2.xStar}$ is feasible, stationarity $1 + 2\lambda x^* = 1 \ne 0$ has no solution, and there is no Slater point. Here $q(\lambda) = \val{D2.tex.q} \to p^*$ as $\lambda \to \infty$, but no $\lambda$ attains it.
\end{itemize}

% ---- duality
\cssec{Duality}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Dual function} $q(\lambda, \nu) = \inf_x \mathcal L(x, \lambda, \nu)$ is concave for every problem (an infimum of affine functions). Dual problem: $d^* = \max_{\lambda \ge 0,\ \nu} q(\lambda, \nu)$.
  \item \textbf{Weak duality}: $q(\lambda, \nu) \le f(x)$ for feasible $x$ and $\lambda \ge 0$, so $d^* \le p^*$ and the duality gap $p^* - d^* \ge 0$. C1: $q(\lambda) = \val{D3.convex.tex.q}$ and $q(\val{ex.weak.lam}) = \val{ex.weak.q} \le p^* = \val{D3.convex.pStar}$.
  \item \textbf{Strong duality}: convex + Slater $\Rightarrow p^* = d^*$. C1: $\max q = q(\val{D3.convex.lamStar}) = \val{D3.convex.dStar} = p^*$, attained at the KKT multiplier $\lambda^*$.
  \item \textbf{Gap without convexity}: $\min x_1x_2 + x_2x_3 + x_1x_3$ subject to $x_i^2 = 1$ has $p^* = \val{D3.bool.pStar}$ and $d^* = \val{D3.bool.tex.dStar}$, a gap of $\val{D3.bool.tex.gap} > 0$.
  \item \textbf{Caveat (S-lemma)}: a problem with a quadratic objective, one quadratic constraint and a strictly feasible point has a zero gap even when nonconvex.
\end{itemize}

% ---- traps
\cssec{Top traps}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Classify eigenvalues $\mu_k$ with a \textbf{relative} tolerance $\varepsilon \max_k |\mu_k|$: an absolute one turns a tiny $H \succ 0$ into zero.
  \item A cross term $c\,x_ix_j$ puts $c$ into \textbf{both} $H_{ij}$ and $H_{ji}$; $c/2$ is the entry of $A$ in $x^\top A x$.
  \item Leading minors decide only $H \succ 0$; $H \succeq 0$ needs \textbf{all} principal minors: $\operatorname{diag}(0, -1)$ has zero leading minors but is not $\succeq 0$.
  \item Simplex: the sort only finds $\theta$; return $\max(v - \theta, 0)$ in the \textbf{original} order. Every coordinate $\le \theta$ vanishes, positive ones too: in B3 $v_1 = \val{B3.params.v.1} > 0$ but $x_1 = 0$.
  \item Signs: $g \le 0$, $+\lambda g$, $\lambda \ge 0$ (SciPy: $c(x) \ge 0$); $\nu$ has no sign; a negative $\lambda$ is not an answer but a wrong active set.
\end{itemize}
